requirements.title: Fire Risk Assessment — Regulatory Reform (Fire Safety) Order 2005
requirements.description: As the occupier of a non-domestic commercial café premises, the sole trader is the 'responsible person' under the Regulatory Reform (Fire Safety) Order 2005. The responsible person must carry out and regularly review a written fire risk assessment covering fire hazards, people at risk, emergency routes/exits, detection and warning systems, firefighting equipment, evacuation plan, and staff information. The assessment must be kept as a written record. The local fire and rescue authority enforces this; penalties include fines up to £5,000 (minor) or unlimited fines and up to 2 years' imprisonment (major).
requirements.authority: Local Fire and Rescue Authority (enforcing Regulatory Reform (Fire Safety) Order 2005)

cost.basis: initial filing — no government fee for the assessment itself; a competent assessor may be hired at commercial cost not determinable from official sources Amount excluded because independent source checks did not support the number.

time.note: No official processing or approval time; operator must carry out the assessment before trading. No registration or approval required — it is a duty, not a licence.

requirements.renewal: Must be reviewed regularly and updated when significant changes occur.
requirements.ongoingFiling: Maintain written record; review regularly.
steps: Carry out a written fire risk assessment of the café premises following the five-step process: identify hazards; identify people at risk; evaluate/remove/reduce risks; record findings and prepare emergency plan; review and update regularly.
Implement appropriate fire safety measures (alarms, extinguishers, emergency exits, signage).
Keep written record available for inspection by fire and rescue authority.
Consider hiring a competent fire risk assessor if lacking expertise.

requirements.title: Allergen Information — Annex II / 14 Major Allergens
requirements.description: Food businesses must provide customers with information on the 14 allergens required to be declared under retained UK food law (derived from EU Regulation 1169/2011 Annex II). These are: celery, cereals containing gluten, crustaceans, eggs, fish, lupin, milk, molluscs, mustard, peanuts, sesame, soybeans, sulphur dioxide/sulphites, and tree nuts. For freshly prepared food sold directly to consumers (non-prepacked), allergen information must be provided orally or in writing at point of service. For prepacked for direct sale (PPDS) food (e.g., packaged sandwiches made and sold on the same premises), full allergen labelling on the packaging is required under Natasha's Law.
